full-bible.subject: Day 1 — Here we go. Genesis.
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Today is the day. You signed up for this. I signed up for this. And right now, a group of us are opening to Genesis 1 together.

Yes, the whole book of Genesis today. Fifty chapters. I am not going to sugarcoat it. That is a lot. But here is what I want you to know. Genesis reads fast. It is all story. Creation, the flood, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Joseph. You will get pulled in.

Do not worry about understanding every detail. Do not stop to study. Just read. Let the words wash over you. You are not writing a paper. You are meeting God in His Word.

If you cannot finish all 50 chapters today, that is okay. Read what you can. Mark where you stopped. Come back to it. The goal is not perfection. The goal is showing up.

I am reading alongside you today.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 2 — Slavery, plagues, and a God who shows up
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Yesterday was Genesis. Today is Exodus. And the tone shifts fast.

The people of God go from favor to slavery in the first chapter. And then God raises up Moses, a man who did not want the job, to lead them out.

Here is what stood out to me when I read this. God did not wait for Moses to be ready. He did not wait for the people to have it together. He showed up because He heard them crying. That was enough.

Today you will read about plagues and Passover and the Red Sea and the Ten Commandments and the building of the tabernacle. It is a full book. Take it one chapter at a time.

You are on Day 2. You showed up again. That matters.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 3 — The one nobody looks forward to
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Leviticus. I know.

This is the book people quit on. All the rules about sacrifices and skin diseases and what to eat and what not to eat. It feels like reading a manual for a world that does not exist anymore.

But here is what I want you to see today. Every single rule in this book exists because God wanted to be close to His people. He was not trying to make their lives harder. He was teaching them how to live near a holy God and survive it.

The whole book is God saying, I want to dwell among you. Here is how.

So push through it. Read it fast if you need to. But do not skip it. There is something in there for you today.

If you are still going after Leviticus, you can handle anything this month throws at you.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 4 — Wandering starts here
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Numbers starts with a census. Then it turns into the story of a people who could not stop complaining.

God had rescued them. Parted the sea. Fed them from the sky. And they still grumbled. They still wanted to go back to Egypt. They still doubted.

And honestly, I see myself in them more than I want to admit.

How many times has God shown up in my life and I still doubted the next thing? How many times has He provided and I still worried about tomorrow?

That is the gift of reading the whole Bible like this. You start to see yourself in the story. Not always in the heroes. Sometimes in the people who could not stop looking back.

Keep going. You are almost through the wilderness.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 5 — Moses says goodbye
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

You have read four books of the Bible this week. And woven through all of them is this idea of rest. In Genesis, God stopped on the seventh day. Not because He was tired. Because He was done, and what He made was good. In Exodus, He told the Israelites not to gather manna on the seventh day. He gave them a double portion on Friday so they would not have to work. Then He put rest right in the middle of the Ten Commandments. Remember the Sabbath. Keep it holy. In Leviticus, the rest went even further. Not just a day but a whole year every seven years. The land needed to breathe too.

Rest is not a reward for finishing your work. It is built into the rhythm God designed from the beginning.

Today is Deuteronomy, and Moses is going to repeat the commandments again. Including the Sabbath. But this time he gives a different reason. In Exodus, God said rest because He rested at creation. In Deuteronomy, Moses says rest because you were slaves in Egypt, and slaves do not get to rest. Rest is what free people do.

You are free. Rest in that today.

Deuteronomy is Moses giving his final speech. He knows he is not going into the Promised Land. He knows his time is almost up. And he spends his last days reminding the people of everything God has done.

Remember. Do not forget. Tell your children. Remember.

He says it over and over. Because he knows what happens when people forget.

Pay attention to the heart behind this book. This is a man who walked with God for forty years, standing at the edge of something he will never see, and his last words are not about himself. They are about making sure the next generation does not lose what matters.

Five days in. Five books down.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 6 — They finally get there
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

After forty years in the wilderness, they cross into the Promised Land. Joshua is in charge now. And the very first thing God says to him is be strong and courageous.

He does not say be smart. He does not say have a plan. He says be strong and do not be afraid.

They made it. Not because they were perfect. Because God kept His promise.

You are almost a week in. Be strong and keep going.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 7 — One week done
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

You have been reading the Bible for a full week. Seven days. That is worth pausing on.

Today is Judges and Ruth. Judges is the story of Israel falling apart. Over and over they turn away from God, things go badly, they cry out, God raises up a judge to save them, and then they do it all again.

And then Ruth shows up. Right in the middle of all that chaos, this quiet little story about faithfulness and kindness and a woman who refused to leave.

One week down. I am proud of you.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 8 — A boy in the temple hears God’s voice
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Today is one of my favorite books. First Samuel. A woman named Hannah prays for a son. God gives her Samuel. She gives him back to God. And then this little boy lying in the temple hears the voice of God and does not even know what it is.

Then you get Saul. Then David. The giant. The friendship with Jonathan. The jealousy. The running. The caves.

First Samuel has everything. It reads like a novel. Enjoy it today.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 9 — David at his best and worst
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Second Samuel is David’s reign. And it is complicated.

The thing that sets David apart is not that he never sinned. It is that he always came back. He repented. He grieved. He did not pretend.

That is the lesson I take from today. Not that I will get it right every time. But that when I do not, I can still come back.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 10 — Solomon builds the temple and then loses his way
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

First Kings starts with Solomon building the most magnificent temple the world had ever seen. And it ends with him worshiping other gods.

You will also meet Elijah today. Standing alone against 450 prophets of Baal. And then running away and hiding under a tree the very next day.

The Bible is honest about people. That is one of the reasons I trust it.

You are ten days in. A third of the way through this challenge.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 11 — Everything falls apart
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Second Kings is hard. You are watching two kingdoms fall. And then Babylon comes. Jerusalem falls. The temple gets destroyed. The people are carried into exile.

It is heavy. But do not rush past the grief of it. This matters.

Some days the reading is going to be hard. Today is one of those days. But you are still here. And that matters.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 12 — The same story, different angle
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

First Chronicles covers a lot of the same ground as Samuel and Kings. But it was written after the exile. When you lose everything and then look back, you see different things. You see the hand of God in places you missed the first time.

Almost two weeks in. You are doing this.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 13 — The rise and fall, one more time
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

And notice the very last verse. Cyrus, king of Persia, lets the people go home. After seventy years of exile, someone opens the door.

God does not forget His promises. Even when it takes seventy years.

Thirteen days. You have read thirteen books of the Bible.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 14 — They go home
full-bible.body:
Good morning. Two weeks in.

All three books are about restoration. About going back to the rubble and building something again. About courage in hard places.

If you are feeling the weight of this challenge right now, these three books are for you today. Broken things get rebuilt. And it starts with one person who says I will go.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 15 — The hardest question in the Bible
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Job. The whole thing. A man who did everything right loses everything. And then God speaks. And He does not answer the question. He just says, I am God and you are not.

We do not always get to know why. We just get to know who.

You are almost halfway through the Bible.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 16 — Halfway. You made it to the Psalms.
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Sixteen days in. You are officially past the halfway mark. And today you land in the Psalms. This is people talking to God. Crying out. Praising. Asking why.

Read them out loud if you can. They were written to be spoken.

Halfway there. I am so proud of you.

Here is my one ask for the second half: tell someone.

Not so you have a buddy to keep you accountable. Tell them because of what this has been for you. If reading the Word this way has meant something, if it has shifted how you see God or how you read the Bible, there is someone in your life who needs that too. Good things are meant to be handed to other people.

You do not even have to find the words. Here is something you can copy, change to sound like you, and post or text to a friend:

"Reading the whole Bible in a month has changed how I read it. Not as individual verses and stories, but the big picture. I am halfway through. You can start any day you want. Come do it with me. heatherlynwilson.com/challenge #31DayBibleChallenge"

Post it, text it, drop it in your group chat. Someone else meeting God in His Word could start with your one sentence.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 17 — More Psalms. Stay with it.
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Psalm 51. David after Bathsheba. Create in me a clean heart, O God.

If you are behind on reading, this is your Psalm 51 moment. Do not quit. Just come back. Read today. That is enough.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 18 — The last of the Psalms
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Psalm 150. Let everything that has breath praise the Lord. After all the crying, the questioning, the doubt, it ends with praise.

You just read the entire book of Psalms in three days. That is remarkable.

Eighteen days down. Thirteen to go.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 19 — Wisdom for the rest of your life
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Proverbs is practical. Ecclesiastes is honest. Song of Solomon is beautiful.

Enjoy today. After the weight of Job and Psalms, this is a different kind of reading.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 20 — The prophet nobody wanted to listen to
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Isaiah is two things at once. Judgment is coming. But a savior is coming too. For unto us a child is born. That is Isaiah 9.

Twenty days. You are almost there.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 21 — Comfort, comfort my people
full-bible.body:
Good morning. Three weeks in.

Comfort, comfort my people. Those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength. He was wounded for our transgressions.

Isaiah wrote these words hundreds of years before Jesus. This might be your favorite day of reading this entire month.

Three weeks done. Ten days left.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 22 — The prophet who did not want the job
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Jeremiah spent his entire life preaching to people who would not listen. And he kept going.

Sometimes faithfulness does not look like success. Sometimes it just looks like showing up.

Nine days left. Keep showing up.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 23 — Jerusalem falls. Jeremiah weeps.
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Great is His faithfulness. His mercies are new every morning.

That verse was not written on a good day. It was written in the ruins. And that is what makes it so powerful.

Mercy is new this morning. For you too.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 24 — Visions, bones, and a valley that comes alive
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Can these bones live? And God says, watch me.

Our God is able to deliver us, but even if He does not, we will not bow.

One week left.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 25 — Twelve books in one day
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Micah tells you what God requires. Do justice. Love mercy. Walk humbly.

Malachi is the last word of the Old Testament. And then silence. Four hundred years of silence.

You just finished the Old Testament. Tomorrow you open to Matthew.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 26 — Jesus is here
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

After everything you have read, all the promises and prophecies and waiting, today you open to the New Testament. The whole story has been leading here.

You have spent 25 days reading about a God who promised He would come. Today He arrives.

Six days left.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 27 — Two more portraits of Jesus
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Luke is the historian. John is the poet. Same Jesus. Completely different angles.

You have now read all four Gospels. Four witnesses. One story. Four days from the finish line.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 28 — The church explodes and Paul changes everything
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Acts reads like an action movie. Shipwrecks. Prison breaks. Miracles. And through all of it, the gospel spreads.

Then Romans. For all have sinned. Nothing can separate us from the love of God.

Three more days.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 29 — Letters to churches that sound like they were written yesterday
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Love is patient. Love is kind. Paul did not write it for weddings. He wrote it for a church that was tearing itself apart.

Galatians is freedom. Ephesians is identity. Philippians is joy from a prison cell.

Two more days.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 30 — One more day after this
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

Hebrews chapter 11 is the faith hall of fame. By faith Abraham. By faith Moses. By faith Rahab. These are your people now. You have read their stories.

One more day. You are going to finish this.

Heather

full-bible.subject: Day 31 — You did it.
full-bible.body:
Good morning.

The Bible ends with a promise. He is making all things new. There will be no more tears. No more death. No more pain.

The story that started in a garden ends in a city. The story that started with God walking with two people ends with God dwelling among all His people forever.

You just read the entire Bible in 31 days.

I am so proud of you. Thank you for reading alongside me.

With love,
Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 1 — Here we go. The story of Jesus starts now.
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Today is the day. You are starting the New Testament and I am reading alongside you.

Matthew opens with a genealogy. Do not skip it. Buried in that list are Rahab, Ruth, and Bathsheba. Women who should not be in the family tree of the Messiah. But they are.

The Sermon on the Mount begins in chapter 5 and it is some of the most powerful teaching you will ever read.

Nine chapters today. You can do this.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 2 — Miracles and hard questions
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Jesus asks the most important question in the entire Bible. Who do you say that I am?

That question is for you too.

You are on Day 2. You showed up again. That is what matters.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 3 — The week that changed everything
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

The last supper. The garden. The betrayal. The cross. The tomb.

And then chapter 28. He is not here. He has risen.

You just finished your first Gospel. Keep going.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 4 — Mark does not slow down
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Mark writes like someone in a hurry to tell you the most important story in the world. Let him.

Day 4. You are building momentum.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 5 — The cross, again. It hits different the second time.
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

You are reading the crucifixion story for the second time in five days. You notice things you missed.

Two Gospels done. You are almost a week in.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 6 — Luke notices the people nobody else sees
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Luke sees the margins. The overlooked. The forgotten. If you have ever felt invisible, Luke’s Gospel is for you.

Six days in. You are finding your rhythm.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 7 — One week done
new-testament.body:
Good morning. One full week.

Martha and Mary. Martha is doing all the work. Mary is sitting at the feet of Jesus. And Jesus says Mary chose the better thing.

You have been reading for seven days straight. Take a breath. You are doing so well.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 8 — Lost things and found things
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

The prodigal son comes home expecting to be a servant. And the father runs to him. Does not wait. Does not lecture. Runs.

That is how God feels about you. Right now. Today.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 9 — The cross, the third time. What do you see now?
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Luke includes things the others do not. The thief on the cross. The road to Emmaus. Sometimes Jesus is right next to you and you do not see it until later.

Three Gospels done.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 10 — John sees something the others did not
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

John is not trying to tell you what Jesus did. He is trying to show you who Jesus is.

Ten days in. One third done.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 11 — I am
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

I am the light of the world. I am the good shepherd. I am the resurrection and the life.

Jesus was not being subtle. He was saying exactly who He was.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 12 — The upper room and the empty tomb
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

I am the vine. Abide in me. I call you friends. I am praying for you.

Four Gospels done. Tomorrow the church begins.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 13 — The Holy Spirit shows up and everything changes
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Peter, the man who denied Jesus, stands up and preaches and three thousand people believe.

Acts is the most exciting book in the New Testament. It reads like an adventure story. Because it is one.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 14 — Two weeks in. Paul enters the story.
new-testament.body:
Good morning. Two weeks.

Saul becomes Paul. Nobody is too far gone. The worst enemy of the church became its greatest champion.

You are halfway through the challenge.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 15 — Missionary journeys and midnight worship
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Paul and Silas singing in a jail cell at midnight. After being beaten. And an earthquake breaks the chains.

That is the power of worship in the dark places.

Fifteen days down.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 16 — Paul will not stop
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

The last word of Acts. Unhindered. The gospel cannot be stopped.

Tomorrow you start Paul’s letters.

Here is my one ask for the second half: tell someone.

Not so you have a buddy to keep you accountable. Tell them because of what this has been for you. If reading the Word this way has meant something, if it has shifted how you see God or how you read the Bible, there is someone in your life who needs that too. Good things are meant to be handed to other people.

You do not even have to find the words. Here is something you can copy, change to sound like you, and post or text to a friend:

"Reading the New Testament in a month has changed how I read it. Not as individual verses and stories, but the big picture. I am halfway through. You can start any day you want. Come do it with me. heatherlynwilson.com/challenge #31DayBibleChallenge"

Post it, text it, drop it in your group chat. Someone else meeting God in His Word could start with your one sentence.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 17 — The deepest theology Paul ever wrote
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Romans 8 might be the single greatest chapter in the entire Bible.

Nothing can separate us from the love of God.

If you only remember one chapter from this entire challenge, make it Romans 8.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 18 — Grace changes everything
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Love sincerely. Hate evil. Be joyful in hope. Patient in affliction. Faithful in prayer.

That is what grace looks like when it hits the ground.

Eighteen down. Keep it.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 19 — Paul writes to a messy church
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Paul does not start by yelling at them. He starts by reminding them who they are.

That is always God’s approach. Before He corrects you, He reminds you who you are.

Twelve days left.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 20 — Love and resurrection
new-testament.body:
Good morning. Twenty days in.

Love is patient. Love is kind. It is not a poem about romance. It is a mirror held up to a church that needed to hear it.

Eleven to go.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 21 — Three weeks. Strength in weakness.
new-testament.body:
Good morning. Three full weeks.

We have this treasure in jars of clay. Fragile. Cracked. Ordinary. But carrying something extraordinary.

The cracks are how the light gets out.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 22 — Freedom
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

It is for freedom that Christ has set us free. Stand firm.

That verse changed my life. Because I am really good at putting chains back on myself that God already removed.

Nine days left.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 23 — Who you are in Christ
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Philippians was written from prison. And it is the most joyful book in the New Testament.

Joy is not about circumstances. It never has been.

Eight days left.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 24 — Letters to friends and a young pastor
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Don’t let anyone look down on you because you are young. Fight the good fight.

One week left.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 25 — Paul’s last letter and a one-page masterpiece
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

I have fought the good fight. I have finished the race. I have kept the faith.

That is how Paul says goodbye.

Six days to go.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 26 — The Old Testament finally makes sense
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Chapter 11 is the faith hall of fame. Chapter 12 says you are surrounded by this great cloud of witnesses cheering you on.

Five days left.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 27 — Faith that does something
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Faith without works is dead. Do not just listen to the word. Do what it says.

Four more days.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 28 — Love. That is the whole thing.
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

God is love. There is no fear in love. Perfect love drives out fear.

Three days left.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 29 — The beginning of the end
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

Holy, holy, holy is the Lord God Almighty, who was and is and is to come.

The story is heading toward worship.

Two more days.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 30 — Hold on. Almost there.
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

The kingdom of the world has become the kingdom of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever.

One more day. Tomorrow you finish.

Heather

new-testament.subject: Day 31 — You did it.
new-testament.body:
Good morning.

He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain. I am making everything new.

You just read the entire New Testament in 31 days.

Thank you for doing this with me. I am so proud of you.

With love,
Heather

james.subject: Day 1 — Read James. All of it. Then pray for wisdom.
james.body:
Good morning.

Welcome to the August challenge. Here is how this works.

Every day for 31 days, you are going to read the entire book of James. All five chapters. Every single day. The same book.

That might sound repetitive. It is supposed to be. Because repetition is how God's Word gets from your head to your heart. By day 10 you will start noticing things you missed. By day 20 you will have pieces memorized without trying. By day 31, James will be part of you.

And every day, after you read, you are going to pray. I will give you a specific prayer focus each morning tied to something in James.

Today's prayer focus is wisdom.

James 1:5 says if any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault, and it will be given to you.

That is your prayer today. Ask God for wisdom. Not for a specific situation unless you have one. Just wisdom. For your day. For your decisions. For the way you treat people. For the words that come out of your mouth.

He gives generously. He does not hold it back. He does not make you earn it. He gives.

Read James. Pray for wisdom. Day 1 is done.

Heather

james.subject: Day 2 — Read James. Pray through the trial you are in.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 1:2 says to consider it pure joy when you face trials of many kinds. That is easy to read. It is not easy to live.

Today as you read James, pay attention to how he talks about trials. He does not say they are fun. He says they produce perseverance. And perseverance produces maturity. There is a purpose in the hard thing.

Your prayer today is about whatever trial you are walking through right now. Big or small. Bring it to God. Not to ask Him to remove it, although you can. But to ask Him what He is building in you through it.

If nothing hard is happening right now, pray for someone you know who is in the middle of something. Text them after. Tell them you prayed.

Day 2. You showed up again.

Heather

james.subject: Day 3 — Read James. Pray about your tongue.
james.body:
Good morning.

James talks about the tongue more than almost anything else. Today I want you to sit with James 1:19. Everyone should be quick to listen, slow to speak, and slow to become angry.

Pray about your words today. Ask God to help you listen more than you talk. Ask Him to slow you down before you react. Ask Him to guard what comes out of your mouth.

This is one of those prayers that will get tested fast. You will probably have an opportunity to be slow to speak before lunch. When it comes, remember you prayed this.

Heather

james.subject: Day 4 — Read James. Pray for the person who frustrates you.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 1:20 says human anger does not produce the righteousness that God desires.

You have someone in your life who frustrates you. We all do. Maybe it is a coworker. A family member. A neighbor. Someone at church. Someone online.

Today, pray for that person. Not a vague prayer. A real one. Pray for their family. Pray for their health. Pray that God would bless them. Pray that He would draw them closer to Himself.

This is one of the hardest prayers you will ever pray. And one of the most freeing. Because you cannot hold anger and intercession in the same hand.

Day 4. Read James. Pray for the hard person.

Heather

james.subject: Day 5 — Read James. Pray about doing, not just hearing.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 1:22. Do not merely listen to the word, and so deceive yourselves. Do what it says.

You have been reading James for five days now. You are starting to know what it says. But knowing and doing are two very different things.

Today, ask God to show you one thing from James that you know but are not doing. Just one. Maybe it is controlling your tongue. Maybe it is showing favoritism. Maybe it is not praying when you should be. Maybe it is talking about tomorrow like you own it.

Ask Him to show you. And then ask Him to help you actually do it. Not tomorrow. Today.

Heather

james.subject: Day 6 — Read James. Pray about favoritism.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 2 opens with a scene. A rich man walks into the room wearing fine clothes and a gold ring. Everyone gives him the best seat. A poor man walks in and gets told to stand in the corner or sit on the floor.

James says if you do this, you have become judges with evil thoughts.

We do this more than we think. We treat people differently based on what they look like, what they drive, what they wear, what they can do for us.

Pray about that today. Ask God to show you where you have been giving the better seat to the wrong people. Ask Him to help you see everyone the way He sees them.

Heather

james.subject: Day 7 — Read James. Pray for your faith to show up in your actions.
james.body:
Good morning. One week in.

James 2:17. Faith by itself, if it is not accompanied by action, is dead.

This is one of the most challenging sentences in the Bible. Because most of us are comfortable with faith as a belief. Something we carry in our hearts. Something we feel. But James says faith that does not move your hands and feet is not really faith at all.

Today, pray that your faith would be visible. Not for show. Not to impress anyone. But because real faith cannot sit still. Ask God where your faith needs legs today. Where does belief need to become action?

Seven days. You have read James seven times. That is the whole book, seven times through.

Heather

james.subject: Day 8 — Read James. Pray about the power of your tongue.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 3. The tongue is a small part of the body, but it makes great boasts. Consider what a great forest is set on fire by a small spark.

You have probably seen this play out. One word ruins a friendship. One sentence changes a marriage. One comment tears down a child's confidence. One text thread destroys a church.

Pray about your tongue today. Not in general. Think about the last week. Was there something you said that you wish you could take back? Was there a conversation where your words were a spark instead of water? Bring that to God.

And ask Him to help you use your words to build today. Every conversation. Every text. Every interaction.

Heather

james.subject: Day 9 — Read James. Pray for peace in a relationship.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 3:17. The wisdom that comes from heaven is first of all pure, then peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial and sincere.

That is the opposite of what the world rewards. The world rewards being right. Being loud. Being first. Winning the argument.

God rewards peace.

Today, pray for peace in a specific relationship. One that has tension in it. One where things are not quite right. Ask God for the kind of wisdom James describes. The kind that leads with peace, not with being right.

Heather

james.subject: Day 10 — Read James. Pray about what you are chasing.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 4:1. What causes fights and quarrels among you? Don't they come from your desires that battle within you?

James does not blame other people for our conflict. He points the finger inward. The fights in your life, the tension, the frustration, a lot of it comes from wanting something you do not have.

Pray about your desires today. Ask God to show you what you have been chasing that is causing conflict. Is it approval? Control? Comfort? Recognition? More money? Being right?

This is not about beating yourself up. This is about honesty. When you can name what you are really chasing, you can bring it to God instead of letting it run your life.

Ten days. You have read James ten times. Things are starting to stick.

Heather

james.subject: Day 11 — Read James. Pray about your pride.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 4:6. God opposes the proud but shows favor to the humble.

I do not want God opposing me. I want Him favoring me. And James is clear about how that works. Humble yourself.

Pride is sneaky. It does not always look like arrogance. Sometimes it looks like not asking for help. Sometimes it looks like refusing to apologize. Sometimes it looks like assuming you already know enough and do not need to learn. Sometimes it looks like thinking you do not really need God today because you have things handled.

Pray about your pride today. Ask God to show you where it has been hiding. And ask Him to replace it with the kind of humility that draws His favor instead of His opposition.

Heather

james.subject: Day 12 — Read James. Pray about submitting to God.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 4:7. Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

We love the second part. Resist the devil and he will flee. But we skip the first part. Submit yourselves to God.

Submission comes first. You cannot resist the enemy if you have not first surrendered to God. The power to stand comes from the posture of kneeling.

Today, pray about surrender. What area of your life are you still holding on to? What have you not given God control of? Your finances? Your relationships? Your career? Your kids? Your plans?

Name it. Give it to Him. Submission is not weakness. It is the starting point of everything James is teaching.

Heather

james.subject: Day 13 — Read James. Pray about judging others.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 4:11. Brothers and sisters, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against a brother or sister or judges them speaks against the law and judges it.

James is not subtle about this. When we judge other people, we are putting ourselves in a seat that belongs to God. There is only one lawgiver and judge. It is not us.

Pray about judgment today. Where have you been looking at someone else's life and making a ruling you were not asked to make? Where have you talked about someone behind their back? Where have you decided you know their motives or their heart?

Ask God to take that out of your hands. It was never yours to carry.

Heather

james.subject: Day 14 — Read James. Pray about tomorrow.
james.body:
Good morning. Two weeks in.

James 4:13. Now listen, you who say, today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business and make money. Why, you do not even know what will happen tomorrow.

We plan. We project. We assume. We talk about next month, next year, five years from now, as if we are in charge of all of it.

James says you do not even know what will happen tomorrow. Instead you should say, if it is the Lord's will, we will live and do this or that.

Pray about your plans today. Not to stop making them. But to hold them loosely. To put God's will above your timeline. To trust that His version of your future is better than the one you have been drawing up.

Two weeks. Halfway there.

Heather

james.subject: Day 15 — Read James. Pray about patience.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 5:7. Be patient, then, brothers and sisters, until the Lord's coming. See how the farmer waits for the land to yield its valuable crop, patiently waiting for the autumn and spring rains.

The farmer does his part. He plants. He tends. But he cannot make it rain. He waits.

There is something in your life right now that you have planted and tended but you cannot make it grow. A prayer you have been praying. A relationship you are hoping will heal. A child who is wandering. A door that has not opened yet.

Pray for patience today. Not passive patience. The kind the farmer has. The kind that keeps tending the field even while waiting for the rain.

Heather

james.subject: Day 16 — Read James. Pray about suffering.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 5:10. Brothers and sisters, as an example of patience in the face of suffering, take the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

The prophets suffered. Job suffered. Jesus suffered. And James points to all of them and says, look at what perseverance produced.

If you are suffering right now, or if someone you love is, pray about it today. Not a polite prayer. A raw one. Tell God where it hurts. Tell Him what you are afraid of. Tell Him what you need.

And then remember what James says at the end. The Lord is full of compassion and mercy. He has not forgotten you.

Heather

james.subject: Day 17 — Read James. Pray a simple yes or no.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 5:12. Let your yes be yes, and your no, no.

This is about integrity. About being the kind of person whose word means something. You do not need to swear by heaven or earth to prove you are telling the truth. Just be honest. Say what you mean. Follow through on what you said you would do.

Pray about your integrity today. Is there something you said you would do that you have not done? Is there a commitment you made that you have been avoiding? Is there a conversation where you were not fully honest?

Ask God to make you a person whose yes means yes. That is rarer than you think.

Heather

james.subject: Day 18 — Read James. Pray for someone who is sick.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 5:14. Is anyone among you sick? Let them call the elders of the church to pray over them.

Prayer for healing is not optional in Scripture. It is not weird. It is not reserved for a certain kind of church. James says do it.

Today, pray for someone who is sick. You know someone. Maybe it is physical. Maybe it is mental. Maybe it is spiritual. Pray specifically. Use their name. Ask God to heal them.

And if that someone is you, ask someone else to pray for you today. That takes courage. But James says the prayer offered in faith will make the sick person well. He did not say the prayer offered alone.

Heather

james.subject: Day 19 — Read James. Confess something to someone you trust.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 5:16. Therefore confess your sins to each other and pray for each other so that you may be healed.

This one is uncomfortable. We like confessing to God because nobody else hears it. But James says confess to each other. Out loud. To another person.

There is something that breaks when you say the thing out loud to someone safe. The shame loses its grip. The secret stops owning you. And healing starts.

Today, pray about whether there is something you need to confess. Not publicly. To one trusted person. A friend who walks with God. A spouse. A mentor. Someone who will not judge you but will pray for you.

If you are not ready to do it today, ask God to make you ready.

Heather

james.subject: Day 20 — Read James. Pray like Elijah.
james.body:
Good morning. Twenty days in.

James 5:17. Elijah was a human being, even as we are. He prayed earnestly that it would not rain, and it did not rain on the land for three and a half years.

James brings up Elijah to make a point. Elijah was not a superhero. He was a person. Just like you. And his prayers moved heaven.

We pray small prayers because we have a small view of what prayer can do. But James says the prayer of a righteous person is powerful and effective. Not might be. Is.

Pray a bold prayer today. Something bigger than what you normally ask for. Something that feels too big. Pray it anyway. Elijah was a human being, even as we are.

Twenty days. You have read James twenty times.

Heather

james.subject: Day 21 — Read James. Pray for someone who has wandered.
james.body:
Good morning. Three weeks.

James ends his entire letter with this. If one of you should wander from the truth and someone should bring that person back, remember this. Whoever turns a sinner from the error of their way will save them from death and cover over a multitude of sins.

The very last thing James writes about is bringing people back. That tells you something about what matters most.

You know someone who has wandered. A friend. A family member. A child. Someone who used to walk with God and does not anymore.

Pray for them by name today. Ask God to draw them back. And ask Him if you are supposed to be part of that. Sometimes bringing someone back starts with a phone call or a text or a meal.

Heather

james.subject: Day 22 — Read James. Pray about temptation.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 1:13. When tempted, no one should say, God is tempting me. For God cannot be tempted by evil, nor does he tempt anyone. But each person is tempted when they are dragged away by their own evil desire and enticed.

James does not let us blame God for our temptation. He does not even let us blame the devil. He says it starts with our own desires. We get dragged away.

Pray about temptation today. Ask God to show you where you are being dragged. What desire is pulling you somewhere you do not want to go? Name it. Bring it into the light. Temptation grows in the dark. It shrinks when you expose it.

Heather

james.subject: Day 23 — Read James. Pray about generosity.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 1:17. Every good and perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of the heavenly lights.

Everything good in your life came from God. Your health. Your family. Your job. Your home. Your next breath. He is the source of every good thing.

When you really believe that, it changes how you hold what you have. If it all came from Him, you can give it freely. You are not the source. You are the pipeline.

Pray about generosity today. Ask God where He wants you to give. Your money, your time, your attention, your encouragement. Ask Him to show you one person who needs something you have. And then go give it.

Heather

james.subject: Day 24 — Read James. Pray about the mirror.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 1:23. Anyone who listens to the word but does not do what it says is like someone who looks at his face in a mirror and, after looking at himself, goes away and immediately forgets what he looks like.

You have been reading James for over three weeks. You know what it says. The question is whether you have been looking in the mirror or walking away from it.

Pray today about what James has shown you about yourself. What have you seen that you have been ignoring? What has convicted you that you have not acted on? What reflection are you walking away from?

Ask God to keep that image in front of you. Not to condemn you. To change you.

Heather

james.subject: Day 25 — Read James. Pray about caring for people who are overlooked.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 1:27. Religion that God our Father accepts as pure and faultless is this. To look after orphans and widows in their distress and to keep oneself from being polluted by the world.

James defines real religion in one sentence. And it is not about church attendance or Bible knowledge or how many worship songs you know. It is about taking care of people who cannot take care of themselves.

Pray about that today. Who in your life is overlooked? Who is alone? Who is struggling and nobody has noticed? Ask God to put someone specific on your heart. And then do something about it.

Six days left.

Heather

james.subject: Day 26 — Read James. Pray about your money.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 5:1. Now listen, you rich people, weep and wail because of the misery that is coming on you.

James is not saying money is evil. He is saying hoarding it is. Holding it while others suffer is. Building your security on it instead of on God is.

Most of us reading this are rich by global standards. We have a roof, food, a phone, access to clean water. We are the ones James is talking to.

Pray about your relationship with money today. Are you holding it too tightly? Are you trusting it more than God? Is there someone who needs what you are sitting on?

This is not about guilt. It is about open hands.

Heather

james.subject: Day 27 — Read James. Pray about heavenly wisdom vs earthly wisdom.
james.body:
Good morning.

James draws a sharp line between two kinds of wisdom.

Earthly wisdom is full of envy, selfish ambition, disorder, and every evil practice. Heavenly wisdom is pure, peace-loving, considerate, submissive, full of mercy and good fruit, impartial, and sincere.

Read that list again. Which one sounds more like your decision-making lately?

Pray for discernment today. Ask God to help you tell the difference between the world's wisdom and His. They can sound similar. The world says look out for yourself. God says look out for others. The world says win the argument. God says make peace. The world says protect your image. God says be sincere.

Four days left.

Heather

james.subject: Day 28 — Read James. Pray about drawing near to God.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 4:8. Come near to God and he will come near to you.

That is one of the most beautiful promises in the Bible. And it is the simplest. You move toward God. He moves toward you. That is it.

You have been reading His Word every single day for almost a month. You have been praying every single day. You have been drawing near. And whether you feel it or not, He has been drawing near to you.

Pray about that today. Thank God for meeting you in this challenge. Thank Him for every morning you showed up and He was already there. Ask Him to keep you close even after this month is over.

Three more days.

Heather

james.subject: Day 29 — Read James. Pray for your church.
james.body:
Good morning.

James was written to a church. Not to individuals sitting alone with their Bibles. To a community of believers who were living together, fighting together, growing together.

Today, pray for your church. Your actual local church. The pastor who is carrying more than you know. The family in the back row who is falling apart and smiling through it. The volunteer who is burning out. The person who stopped showing up and nobody called.

Pray that your church would look like what James describes. No favoritism. Faith with action. Tamed tongues. Heavenly wisdom. Prayers for the sick. Confession and healing.

Two more days.

Heather

james.subject: Day 30 — Read James. Pray about what has changed in you.
james.body:
Good morning.

James 1:4. Let perseverance finish its work so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.

You have read James thirty times. Thirty. You have prayed with focus and intention every single day. That is perseverance. And perseverance has been doing its work in you whether you see it or not.

Today, pray about what has changed. Ask God to show you. Maybe your tongue has been slower. Maybe your prayers have been bolder. Maybe you have been more generous or more patient or more aware of people around you.

Something shifted this month. Take a minute to thank God for it.

One more day.

Heather

james.subject: Day 31 — You did it. One last time through James.
james.body:
Good morning.

Day 31. The last day.

Read James one more time. The whole book. But today, read it slow. You know these words now. They are not new anymore. They are yours.

And today, pray about whatever God puts on your heart. No prompt from me. No specific verse. Just you and Him and the book you have spent a month inside of.

You read James thirty-one times. You prayed with intention every single day. You showed up when it was hard, when you were tired, when you did not feel like it.

James says be doers of the word. You have been. Not perfectly. But faithfully. And faithful is what God is looking for.

I am so proud of you. Thank you for doing this with me.

What is next? Keep reading. Keep praying. Keep showing up. That is the whole thing.

With love,
Heather

beatitudes.title: Where we are headed
beatitudes.practice: Read Matthew 5:1-12 out loud three times. That is all today.
beatitudes.body:
Welcome to the first day. For the next 30 days we are going to hide the Beatitudes in our hearts, one line at a time, until we can say the whole thing from memory.

Jesus saw the crowds, went up on the mountainside, and sat down to teach. The first thing out of His mouth was not a rule. It was a list of who is blessed. And almost every person on the list is someone the world would overlook. The poor in spirit. The mourning. The meek. This is the upside down kingdom, and we are going to carry it in our hearts.

Today, just read the whole passage a few times. Do not try to memorize anything yet. Let it wash over you. Tomorrow we start with the very first line.

beatitudes.title: Poor in spirit
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3 ten times today. Once when you wake up, and again every time you get a drink of water.
beatitudes.body:
Here is our first line to learn: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

Poor in spirit does not mean poor in money. It means knowing you are empty without God. It is the person who has stopped pretending they have it all together and finally admits they need Him. That is where the kingdom begins. Not with the strong and self-made, but with the ones honest enough to say I cannot do this on my own.

God is not looking for people who are impressive. He is looking for people who are open. Emptiness is not a problem to Him. It is the doorway.

beatitudes.title: Poor in spirit, in real life
beatitudes.practice: Cover part of the verse in the practice game and fill in the rest from memory. Then say it once more before bed.
beatitudes.body:
Being poor in spirit shows up in ordinary moments. It is the prayer you whisper when you do not know what to do. It is asking for help instead of white knuckling it. It is the relief of stopping the performance.

The world tells us to be self-sufficient, to never let them see you struggle. Jesus says the ones who admit their need are the ones who get the whole kingdom. What a trade.

Where in your life are you still pretending to be fine? That is exactly where He wants to meet you.

beatitudes.title: Lock in the first line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3 from memory five times. Try writing it on a sticky note and putting it on your mirror.
beatitudes.body:
Today we make the first line stick. You should be able to say Matthew 5:3 without looking now, or close to it.

Here is a memory trick that works: attach the words to a picture. Picture an empty cupped hand held open, waiting to be filled. Poor in spirit, hands open, kingdom poured in. Your brain remembers pictures long after it forgets words.

One down. Seven to go. You are already building something.

beatitudes.title: Those who mourn
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:4 to your practice. Then say verses 3 and 4 back to back.
beatitudes.body:
The second line: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.

This one is tender. Jesus does not skip over grief or rush us past it. He blesses it. He says the ones who mourn are not forgotten, they are comforted. There is a kind of sorrow that softens us instead of hardening us, that turns us toward God instead of away.

We mourn our own sin. We mourn a broken world. We mourn people we have lost. And into all of it, God does not say get over it. He says I will comfort you.

beatitudes.title: Comfort that actually comes
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 and 4 together from memory. Notice how they start the same way. That pattern is your friend.
beatitudes.body:
The promise is not that we will avoid grief. It is that grief will not get the last word. Comfort comes. Sometimes through Scripture, sometimes through a friend who shows up, sometimes through a peace you cannot explain.

If you are in a hard season right now, this verse is for you. You are not being punished. You are being carried. The comfort is on its way, and often it comes in the middle of the mourning, not only after.

Do not hide your tears from God. He counts them.

beatitudes.title: Lock in the second line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3 and 5:4 from memory three times. Play the hide game and push the difficulty up one notch.
beatitudes.body:
Two lines down. Every Beatitude starts with Blessed are, and that repetition is doing the heavy lifting for your memory. Lean on it.

Try saying both verses out loud in the car today. Something about saying it while you drive locks it in. No one is watching. Just you and the words.

You are one quarter of the way to the kingdom list living in your heart.

beatitudes.title: The meek
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:5. Say verses 3, 4, and 5 in order.
beatitudes.body:
Line three: Blessed are the meek, for they will inherit the earth.

Meek is one of the most misunderstood words in the Bible. It does not mean weak. It means strength under control. Think of a powerful horse that has learned to be gentle. The meek are not pushovers. They are people who could push back and choose not to, because they trust God to handle it.

The world says grab everything you can. Jesus says the gentle ones inherit it all in the end. You do not have to claw your way to the top. You can trust the One who owns the earth.

beatitudes.title: Strength that stays gentle
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 through 5 from memory. Use the hide game to check yourself.
beatitudes.body:
Meekness is the mom who could yell but kneels down instead. It is the person in the meeting who could win the argument but keeps the peace. It is choosing gentleness when you have every right to come out swinging.

That kind of restraint is not weakness. It takes more strength than lashing out ever did. And Jesus says it is the meek, not the loud, who inherit the earth.

Who in your life needs your gentleness today, especially when they do not deserve it?

beatitudes.title: Lock in the third line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-5 from memory five times. Print a card from the resources and put it somewhere you will see it.
beatitudes.body:
Three down. You now have poor in spirit, mourn, meek. Notice they build on each other. First you know your need, then you grieve what is broken, then you hold your strength gently. There is an order to becoming like Jesus.

This is a good day to write all three on a card and tape it somewhere you look every day. The fridge. The bathroom mirror. Your car dashboard.

beatitudes.title: Hunger and thirst
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:6. Say verses 3 through 6 in order.
beatitudes.body:
Line four: Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.

We are at the center of the list now. Hunger and thirst are not casual wants. They are needs you feel in your body. Jesus is describing people who want to be right with God and want to see the world made right the way a starving person wants food.

And the promise is stunning. They will be filled. God never starves a hungry heart. If you actually want more of Him, that desire itself is a gift, and He will not leave it empty.

beatitudes.title: What you hunger for
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 through 6 from memory. You are at the halfway point of the eight.
beatitudes.body:
We hunger for a lot of things that never fill us. More stuff, more approval, more scrolling. We keep eating and stay hungry. Jesus points to the one hunger that actually gets satisfied, wanting to be right with God.

Here is the good news hiding in this verse. You do not have to manufacture righteousness. You just have to want it. The wanting is the doorway. He does the filling.

What have you been trying to fill up on lately that has left you empty?

beatitudes.title: Lock in the fourth line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-6 from memory. Then try saying it to another person out loud, even a kid.
beatitudes.body:
Four down, four to go. You are halfway. Take a second to be proud of that. Two weeks ago these were words on a page, and now they live in you.

Today, try reciting all four without looking at all. If you get stuck, that is fine. Getting stuck and pushing through is exactly how memory gets strong. The struggle is the workout.

beatitudes.title: The merciful
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:7. Say verses 3 through 7 in order.
beatitudes.body:
Line five: Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.

Mercy is love with its sleeves rolled up. It is not just feeling bad for someone, it is doing something about it. Forgiving the debt. Making the meal. Giving the second chance you were not obligated to give.

And notice the return. The merciful will be shown mercy. This is not earning God's mercy, we already have it. It is that mercy given has a way of flowing back to you. The hand that gives is the hand that receives.

beatitudes.title: Mercy in action
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 through 7 from memory. Show one act of mercy to someone today, even a small one.
beatitudes.body:
Mercy usually costs something. Time, money, pride, the right to be right. That is what makes it mercy and not just being nice. Jesus was merciful all the way to a cross.

We find it easy to want mercy for ourselves and justice for everyone else. This verse flips that. Be the one who gives the grace you hope to receive.

Is there someone you have been holding a debt against? Today might be the day to let it go.

beatitudes.title: Lock in the fifth line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-7 from memory while doing a chore. Push the hide game up a level.
beatitudes.body:
Five down. Look how far you have come. Poor in spirit, mourn, meek, hunger and thirst, merciful. You are carrying more than half of the Beatitudes in your heart now.

A good test today. Say them while you are doing something else, folding laundry, walking, driving. If you can say them with your hands busy, they are becoming part of you, not just something you recite.

beatitudes.title: The pure in heart
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:8. Say verses 3 through 8 in order.
beatitudes.body:
Line six: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.

Pure in heart means undivided. It is a heart that is not split between God and a hundred other loyalties. Not perfect, but honest. No hidden rooms, no secret self. What you see is what is really there.

And the promise is the greatest one yet. They will see God. Purity is not about being good enough to earn a look at Him. It is that a clean window lets the light through. When our hearts are undivided, we finally see Him clearly.

beatitudes.title: An undivided heart
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 through 8 from memory. Sit quiet for one minute and ask God to make your heart undivided.
beatitudes.body:
A divided heart is exhausting. Trying to serve God and also protect an image, chase approval, and keep a secret all at once will wear you out. Jesus offers something simpler. One heart, pointed one way.

Purity of heart is not about never messing up. It is about not hiding when you do. It is bringing the whole self into the light, even the parts you are ashamed of. That is where you see God most clearly, in the honesty.

Is there a corner of your heart you have kept in the dark? He is gentle. Bring it to Him.

beatitudes.title: Lock in the sixth line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-8 from memory. Teach one verse to someone younger than you.
beatitudes.body:
Six down. Only two more Beatitudes to learn. You are so close to having the whole list.

Here is a fun one for today. If you have kids around, teach them verse 8. Kids memorize fast, and teaching someone else is the best way to cement it in your own mind. Make it a little game at dinner.

beatitudes.title: The peacemakers
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:9. Say verses 3 through 9 in order.
beatitudes.body:
Line seven: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

Notice it says peacemakers, not peacekeepers. Keeping the peace often means avoiding, staying quiet, letting things slide. Making peace is active. It steps into the mess and works to reconcile. It costs something.

And look at the reward. They will be called children of God. When you make peace, you look like your Father, because that is exactly what He did for us through Jesus. Peacemaking is the family resemblance.

beatitudes.title: Make peace, do not just keep it
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 through 9 from memory. Take one step toward peace with someone today.
beatitudes.body:
Peacemaking is hard because it usually means going first. Being the one to apologize, to reach out, to break the silence. It is easier to keep score. But Jesus blesses the ones who lay down the scorecard and build a bridge.

This does not mean pretending everything is fine. Real peace deals with the real thing. It is honest and kind at the same time.

Is there a relationship where you could go first this week?

beatitudes.title: Lock in the seventh line
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-9 from memory twice. Spend extra time on any line that trips you up.
beatitudes.body:
Seven down. One Beatitude left. You can almost say the whole thing.

You are at the level now where the hide game should be covering half the words and you can still fill them in. If that feels hard, that is normal. Keep going back to the ones that trip you up. Those sticky spots just need a few more reps.

beatitudes.title: The persecuted
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:10. You now have all eight. Say verses 3 through 10 in order.
beatitudes.body:
The eighth and final line: Blessed are those who are persecuted because of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.

This is the hard one. Jesus is honest that doing the right thing sometimes costs you. People may misunderstand you, push back, even turn on you. He does not promise the Christian life will be easy. He promises it will be worth it.

And look, the list ends where it began. Theirs is the kingdom of heaven. The very same reward as the poor in spirit. The circle closes. Blessing at the start, blessing at the end.

beatitudes.title: Blessed when it costs you
beatitudes.practice: Say verses 3 through 10 from memory. That is all eight Beatitudes. Sit with that for a second.
beatitudes.body:
Most of us will not face real persecution. But we all know the smaller version, being left out, laughed at, or judged for doing what is right. Jesus sees it, and He calls it blessed.

The reward is not someday only. It is theirs, present tense, the kingdom of heaven belongs to them right now. When standing for what is right costs you, you are not losing. You are in good company, and the kingdom is yours.

Have you ever paid a price for doing the right thing? Jesus saw it.

beatitudes.title: Lock in all eight
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-10 from memory three times. Smooth out the rough spots.
beatitudes.body:
You did it. All eight Beatitudes are in your heart. Today is not about learning a new line, it is about running the whole list until it flows.

Say them start to finish. Then again. Then again. Each time it gets a little smoother. The goal is not just to recall them but to be able to say them like you mean them, because you do.

Tomorrow we add the last piece Jesus said, the part where He turns and speaks straight to you.

beatitudes.title: When they say all kinds of evil
beatitudes.practice: Add Matthew 5:11-12. Say the entire passage, verses 3 through 12, from memory.
beatitudes.body:
After the eight, Jesus turns personal. He stops saying blessed are they and starts saying blessed are you. Verses 11 and 12: Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you and falsely say all kinds of evil against you because of me. Rejoice and be glad, because great is your reward in heaven.

This is Jesus looking right at you. When it comes, and it may, His instruction is almost shocking. Rejoice. Be glad. Not because the pain is not real, but because you are in the long line of prophets who stood for God and the reward is huge.

Add these two verses to your recitation. Now you have the whole passage.

beatitudes.title: Put it all together
beatitudes.practice: Say Matthew 5:3-12 from memory. Try making up a simple tune for it, or walking while you say it.
beatitudes.body:
You have every piece now. Today we make it one smooth thing instead of nine separate parts.

Here is a tip. Say it with your body. Some people walk while they recite. Some tap the rhythm. Some have made up a simple tune and sing it, and honestly that is the fastest way of all. If a song helps you, make one up and do not overthink it. Nobody has to hear it but you and God.

Run the whole passage a few times today. You are almost there.

beatitudes.title: Say it without looking
beatitudes.practice: Play the hide game at the hardest level you can. Say the whole passage out loud twice.
beatitudes.body:
Today, close the book and say the whole thing. When you hit a wall, do not peek right away. Sit in it for a second and let your memory reach for it. That reaching is what makes it permanent.

Most of the words are hidden in the practice game now. If you can fill in eighty percent from memory, you are ready for the home stretch.

You have carried this passage for almost a month. It is becoming part of who you are.

beatitudes.title: Almost there
beatitudes.practice: Recite Matthew 5:3-12 to one other person, out loud, from memory.
beatitudes.body:
One day before the finish. Today, say the entire passage to another person. Your spouse, your kid, a friend, whoever. Saying it out loud to a real face is different than saying it alone, and it will show you how solid it really is.

Do not worry about being perfect. Worry about meaning it. These are not just words you memorized. This is the heart of Jesus, and it is in you now.

Tomorrow is the celebration, and your challenge to share it.

beatitudes.title: You hid it in your heart
beatitudes.practice: Record yourself saying Matthew 5:3-12 from memory. Share it with #HideItInYourHeart, then open your certificate.
beatitudes.body:
Thirty days ago these were words on a page. Today they live in you. That is a real thing, and it does not go away. You have hidden the Beatitudes in your heart, and no one can take them.

Here is the final challenge, and it is a fun one. Record yourself saying the whole passage from memory. Just your phone, no need to be polished. Then share it. Post it on your dashboard here, and put it on Facebook or Instagram with the hashtag HideItInYourHeart. Your recording might be the nudge that gets someone else to start.

Then grab your certificate. You earned every word of it. I am so proud of you.
